clue.text: Strictly speaking, FT when not abbreviated?

definitions.text: Strictly speaking, FT when not abbreviated?

parts.words: Strictly speaking, FT when not abbreviated?
parts.note: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC TV show; FT, written out in full in a dance programme, is foxtrot, a step on its floor, not the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A pedant insists that FT, the newspaper's initials, be spelt out in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strictly' is the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing, and FT is the short form of foxtrot, so speaking of the show, FT unabbreviated is a step of this kind of dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxtrot is a standard dance of the kind performed on Strictly, so the whole clue describes formal partnered dancing in a hall.

clue.text: Virginia's set flowers put in ground to develop, taking week

parts.note: blooms are flowers
to bury something is to put it in the ground

indicators.note: taking means taking away, so the letter for week is removed from the phrase for develop

parts.note: to develop is to grow up

explanation.surface: Someone sets flowers in the ground to grow on for a week, while Virginia watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' means taking away: W comes out of GROW UP, leaving GROUP. 'To' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf was a leading member of this circle of London writers, artists and thinkers, named after a district of central London.

clue.text: The smallest room (new loft) advertised in Barking?

indicators.note: advertised means announced or proclaimed, so these words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the smallest room is a jocular British name for the toilet, a loo; new is N; a loft is an attic: loo, N, attic run together

explanation.surface: An estate agent's listing: a converted loft with its own toilet, offered in Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, LOO-N-ATTIC gives the answer. Barking is a real district of east London, which disguises its sense of mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for insane, so a mad person fits.

clue.text: Crushes, squeezes olives after making extra virgin oil

definitions.meaning: to crush a rebellion or a feeling is to hold it down by force

definitions.text: squeezes olives after making extra virgin oil
definitions.meaning: extra virgin oil comes from the first pressing, so squeezing the olives afterwards is pressing them again

explanation.surface: An olive grower presses the fruit a second time after the prized first oil is out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RE-PRESSES to read the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: subduing or stifling something, and pressing a second time once the first-press oil has been drawn off.

clue.text: Oscar's gloomy hum

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's (is) links it to the next piece
dour means gloomy or stern

explanation.surface: Oscar is humming a gloomy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' is not a sound here but British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hum is a smell, usually an unpleasant one, so a scent or whiff fits.

clue.text: Knockdown compost?

parts.note: a knockdown price is a very low one; compost is a kind of soil, so it might whimsically be called cheap soil

explanation.surface: A garden centre clearance sale on bags of compost.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted the clue was whimsical: compost is dirt, and at a knockdown price it is cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockdown prices are extremely low, and the phrase means costing very little indeed.

clue.text: Spirited girl has my back in northern pub

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the pair of letters for northern and pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: back means the word my is read backwards

explanation.surface: A lively girl sits with her back to the speaker in a northern pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the word my, and 'in' places it inside the abbreviations for northern and pub. 'Spirited' sounds like lively but means literally a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a nature spirit taking the form of a young woman, so a girl who is literally a spirit.

clue.text: Contrary writing style of McGonagall?

definitions.meaning: contrary means opposite, turned the other way
William McGonagall was a Scottish poet famed as the worst in the language; he wrote in metre and rhyme

explanation.surface: A reader complains that the poet McGonagall's style goes against all good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN VERSE for the second sense: William McGonagall, a Victorian Scot, is remembered for dreadful poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite or reversed in order is the mathematical and general sense; a poet's work is written in metrical lines.

clue.text: Jason the bird collector?

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Jason went on a quest to bring back the Golden Fleece
a gun dog that fetches shot game birds for the hunter

explanation.surface: Someone called Jason is described as a collector of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Jason fetched back the Golden Fleece, so he was literally a retriever of something golden; the dog breed collects shot birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a gun dog bred to fetch game, and Jason of the Argonauts brought home the golden fleece.

clue.text: Take responsibility over angry putdown alienating daughter

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: angry suggests letters thrown into turmoil, so these are rearranged
alienating means pushing away, so the daughter's letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone must accept blame for a furious insult that drove a daughter away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alienating' removes the daughter's D from putdown, and 'angry' rearranges what is left, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit to something is to accept that one did it, owning the blame.

clue.text: Marvel production featuring Magneto's ultimate elimination

indicators.note: a production is something made or put together, so these letters are reworked
ultimate means last, so the final letter of Magneto is taken

explanation.surface: A Marvel film features the villain Magneto's final defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production' rearranges MARVEL plus O, the last letter of Magneto. 'Featuring' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something away gets rid of it, which is what elimination means.

clue.text: Send cycling headgear for the bishop!

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other, here the front two to the back

parts.note: to remit is to send, as money

explanation.surface: An order to cycle over with a bishop's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves RE from the front of REMIT to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed hat is a bishop's ceremonial headdress.

clue.text: Maybe sprinter; or chaser, jumping the last at Aintree?

indicators.note: jumping suggests letters leaping about into a new order
the last letter of the word Aintree is taken

explanation.surface: Speculation on whether an animal is a flat sprinter or a steeplechaser jumping the final fence at Aintree, the Grand National course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping' rearranges OR CHASER plus E. 'Maybe' says a sprinter is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter in racing is a horse that runs over short distances, one example of a thoroughbred bred to run.

clue.text: Relapse, injecting a bit of laudanum into bottom

indicators.note: injecting signals one piece being put inside another
into shows where the small piece goes, inside the word for bottom

parts.note: backside is an informal word for bottom

indicators.note: a bit of picks out only the first letter of laudanum

explanation.surface: An addict slides back into the habit, injecting opiates into the buttocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injecting ... into' puts L inside BACKSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lapse back into old bad habits is to slip from progress, a synonym.

clue.text: Take on debts having no interest?

parts.note: to incur a cost is to take it on
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A borrower takes on debts at zero interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial, but it means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking curiosity means not caring to know more, having no interest in things.

clue.text: France left the single currency, mademoiselle

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
EUR is the code for the euro, Europe's single currency

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman: France has quit the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A mademoiselle is a young Frenchwoman, and this is a French girl's name, one example.

clue.text: Evergreens split unfortunately, somewhere in the field

parts.note: firs are evergreen conifers

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Fir trees have split badly somewhere out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges split. The field is a cricket field, where fielding positions have names.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is the fielding position beside the wicketkeeper on the off side, one spot in the field.

clue.text: Problem covered up by Gore Bush?

indicators.note: covered up by means the letters sit concealed inside the words Gore Bush

explanation.surface: A problem hushed up by Al Gore and George Bush, rivals for the 2000 US presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle in which images and letters stand for words is a kind of problem to solve.

clue.text: Rudely enter boozer, loudly demanding gin

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar

indicators.note: loudly demanding means the word is heard called out, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: the spirit gin, called for aloud across the bar, is heard as the second half of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone storms into the pub shouting for gin.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR, then GEIN spoken sounds like gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude abruptly or rudely is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Policeman fit to guard Yard's exclusive property

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the letter for yard goes inside

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
right means fit, as in right as rain
Y is the standard abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A fit officer is assigned to guard Scotland Yard's private property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard but is only Y.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the legal right owned exclusively by a creator over their work, a form of intellectual property.

clue.text: Make love tonight raunchily, ecstasy-fuelled having ditched husband

indicators.note: raunchily suggests wild, unruly behaviour, so the letters are rearranged
having ditched means the letter for husband is dropped

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A wild night planned on drugs, with the husband out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having ditched' takes H from TONIGHT; 'raunchily' rearranges TONIGT plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for having sex, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Government criteria adapted in relation to senior citizens

indicators.note: adapted means changed to fit, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The government changes its eligibility rules for pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the elderly and their care, relating to old age.

clue.text: Morning spent with Italy's foremost instrument maker

parts.note: at means spent with, as in time at a friend's

indicators.note: foremost picks out the first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: A morning passed in the company of Italy's leading violin maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of Cremona luthiers made celebrated violins before Stradivari, so a maker of stringed instruments.

clue.text: Minute interval caught before bullets getting fired back?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: fired back means the word for bullets is sent the other way, read backwards

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition, bullets

explanation.surface: A brief pause before the bullets come flying back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just orders C first. A comma in music is a minute interval of pitch, while in text it marks a short pause.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory this is a tiny difference in pitch between two notes, a very small interval.

clue.text: African boy king is back

parts.note: Tutankhamun, known as King Tut, was the boy king of Egypt

indicators.note: back means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: An African boy-king makes a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Leaves no-go area, endlessly troubled

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endlessly means the final letter of the phrase is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone quits a dangerous no-go area beset by unending trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun: herb leaves. 'Endlessly' drops the last A; 'troubled' rearranges NOGOARE.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is used as dried leaves in cooking, an example.

clue.text: Cocktail namer who gave us the Flaming Ferrari?

definitions.text: Cocktail namer who gave us the Flaming Ferrari?

parts.words: Cocktail namer who gave us the Flaming Ferrari?
parts.note: a Flaming Ferrari is a drink set alight; the improvised petrol bomb is named after a Soviet foreign minister

explanation.surface: Who invented the Flaming Ferrari, a cocktail that is set on fire?
explanation.walkthrough: The firebomb was named after Vyacheslav Molotov, Soviet foreign minister, mocked by the Finns in 1939; a flaming bottle is a cocktail in that sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet politician gave his surname to the petrol bomb known as a cocktail.

clue.text: It helps writer to come to the point

definitions.text: It helps writer to come to the point

parts.words: It helps writer to come to the point
parts.note: coming to the point usually means getting to the matter, but here a tool literally puts a point on a writing implement

explanation.surface: Advice on helping a rambling author get to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A small device that sharpens a pencil puts a fresh point on a writing tool.
